lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constructing linear and exponential functions from data
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: constructing linear and exponential functions from data

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 9, 36, 144, 576. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.

items.prompt: A population of 1100 grows by 11% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 5 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 64 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
A stays ahead permanently because 64 is larger than 3.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2800(0.96)^t, with t in years. What does 0.96 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $2800
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.96, meaning a 4% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (2, 5) and (7, 0). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 9, 13, 17, 21. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.

items.prompt: A population of 1100 grows by 11% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 8 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 42 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
A stays ahead permanently because 42 is larger than 3.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
